slots.name: stolen bottles
slots.sentence: Marchesi Antinori, one of Italy’s most renowned winemakers, on Friday said 30,000 bottles of some of its most prized wine varieties were stolen.

slots.name: loss value
slots.sentence: Thieves stole thousands of bottles of wine worth around $5.6 million from a vineyard in Tuscany in one of the largest, most audacious wine heists in recent history.

slots.name: masked people
slots.sentence: Seven masked people entered an Antinori warehouse in the Tuscan town of Cortona last weekend and loaded two large trucks with the bottles, which had been packed and assembled in preparation for being shipped to foreign markets, said Renzo Cotarella, the company’s chief executive.

slots.name: trucks used
slots.sentence: The thieves shut off the alarm, forced open a gate and used the firm’s own forklifts to lift the wine crates and load them into the trucks, Cotarella said.

slots.name: investigation status
slots.sentence: In the Marchesi Antinori case, three varieties of premium red wine were stolen: Solaia, Guado al Tasso and Tignanello, all from the firm’s highly praised 2023 vintage.

slots.name: wine varieties
slots.sentence: The retail price of a bottle of Solaia is between $450 and $560.

slots.name: bottles per variety
slots.sentence: The CEO added that company workers discovered the theft on Monday morning, when the shipments were supposed to move.

slots.name: export countries
slots.sentence: The company, which exports to 170 countries, on Friday warned importers against buying potentially stolen products.

slots.name: prior robberies
slots.sentence: The company was caught off guard: Antinori had never experienced a robbery before, Cotarella said.
